title: OpenSurvey Survey Definition
description: FROZEN Wave-0 contract. Single source of truth for the Survey.questions array, per-question declarative logic, survey-level config (languages/status/close/styling), the segment filter, and answer value shapes. Consumed by: the React runtime (TS), the React builder (TS), and Django (Python jsonschema). Every user-facing display string is an i18n map {langCode: text}. Enum string values MUST match contracts/models.md PART C and contracts/openapi.yaml.
$comment: Top-level object validates a full Survey definition payload. Survey.questions == #/properties/questions; Survey.languages == #/properties/languages; Survey.styling == #/properties/styling; Survey.close_on == #/properties/closeConditions. Segment.filter validates against #/$defs/segmentFilter.

endings.description: One or more ending/thank-you screens. action 'end-survey' may target a specific ending by id.

followUps.description: Survey-level follow-up automations (the editor's 4th 'Follow-ups' tab). Each entry fires an action when a response is finalized, optionally gated by a condition over the answers. Mirrors how `endings` is defined: a re-broadcast array of #/$defs/followUp. Server-persisted on Survey.follow_ups (JSONField default=[]); the snake_case body key is `follow_ups` -> validated as `followUps` (additionalProperties:false on the item), exactly like welcome_card -> welcomeCard.

blocks.description: OPTIONAL question-grouping overlay (the editor's 'Block 1..N' grouping). ADDITIVE + backward-compatible: an absent/empty `blocks` array == today's exact FLAT behavior. The FLAT `questions[]` array remains the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for flow order + logic resolution — blocks NEVER move questions inside the schema and NEVER reorder `questions[]`. A block is purely a DISPLAY GROUPING (the builder lists its member questions together) plus an optional WITHIN-BLOCK randomization of the order those member questions are PRESENTED at runtime (seeded per-response so back-nav is stable). The same key on the wire in both the admin body and the model column (`blocks` -> `blocks`, no snake/camel rename), so it needs no _SNAKE_TO_SCHEMA_KEY entry — unlike welcome_card/hidden_fields/follow_ups. Cross-references (every questionId resolves to a real question; a question appears in at most one block; unique block ids) cannot be expressed in jsonschema and are enforced in-code by apps.surveys.blocks_validation.validate_blocks (mirroring apps.followups.validation.validate_follow_ups). DEFERRED (noted, out of scope to bound risk): block-level LOGIC. Server-persisted on Survey.blocks (JSONField default=[]; mirrors `endings`).

variables.description: OPTIONAL author-defined survey variables (Formbricks parity). ADDITIVE + backward-compatible: an absent/empty `variables` array == today's exact behavior (no variable replay). Each variable is a named, typed mutable value (number | text) seeded from `initialValue`. A NEW `calculate` logic action (#/$defs/action) mutates a variable as the respondent progresses; recall/piping + conditions can READ a variable value by its id (variables share the question/ending/hidden-field id namespace, so a recall token `#recall:<varId>/...#` and a condition `leftQuestionId: <varId>` both resolve to the variable's live value). Variables are computed deterministically at runtime by replaying the matching `calculate` actions along the answered path (apps.surveys.logic.compute_variables + its TS twin) — they are NOT persisted into Response.data. The same key on the wire in both the admin body and the model column (`variables` -> `variables`, no snake/camel rename). Cross-references (unique variable ids across the question/ending/hidden-field/variable namespace; `calculate.variableId` resolves; type-compatible operation; ref values resolve; a condition leaf referencing a variable uses a type-valid operator) cannot be expressed in jsonschema and are enforced in-code by apps.surveys.logic.validate_survey (the same in-code validator that owns the unique-id + operator/type checks; variables are intrinsic to the logic evaluator, so they live there rather than in a separate module — mirrored line-for-line by the TS validateSurvey). Server-persisted on Survey.variables (JSONField default=[]; mirrors `endings`).

quotas.description: OPTIONAL response quotas (Formbricks parity). ADDITIVE + backward-compatible: an absent/empty `quotas` array == today's exact behavior (no quota enforcement). Each quota caps how many FINISHED responses matching a `condition` (a #/$defs/conditionGroup — the SAME shape logic rules + follow-ups use) are accepted; once the cap is hit, the (Nth+1) matching respondent is marked OVER-QUOTA at finalize and the runtime shows the quota's `endingId` (or a built-in 'quota full' screen when `endingId` is absent). Enforcement lives in apps.responses.public_services.finalize_response (a hook alongside the webhook/follow-up dispatch); the condition is evaluated by the SAME frozen evaluator as logic (apps.surveys.logic._eval_condition) against the final Response.data (no variable replay) — ZERO drift with logic gating. The same key on the wire in both the admin body and the model column (`quotas` -> `quotas`, no snake/camel rename). Cross-references (unique quota ids; `endingId` resolves to a declared endings[].id; condition `leftQuestionId` refs resolve to a real question/hidden-field id with a type-valid operator) cannot be expressed in jsonschema and are enforced in-code by apps.surveys.quotas_validation.validate_quotas (mirroring apps.followups.validation.validate_follow_ups). NOT exposed on the public runtime serializer — quota conditions are server-only (never leaked to respondents). Server-persisted on Survey.quotas (JSONField default=[]; mirrors `endings`).

langCode.description: BCP-47-ish language code, or the literal 'default'. Must equal a Language.code declared in survey.languages, OR the reserved 'default'.

i18nString.description: A localized display string: map of langCode -> text. MUST contain the 'default' key (the fallback shown when a response language has no entry). Every user-facing string in this schema uses this type. RECALL/PIPING: a headline/subheader string MAY embed recall tokens of the FROZEN form `#recall:<id>/fallback:<text>#`, where <id> is an EARLIER question id or a hiddenFields[].id, and <text> is shown when that source is unanswered (the fallback text may not contain '#'). Tokens are plain text to jsonschema (they validate as ordinary strings) and are resolved at render time by the shared resolveRecall() helper in BOTH the runtime and the builder preview.

i18nStringOptional.$comment: Same as i18nString but the 'default' key is not required (for optional subtitles/placeholders).

questionId.description: Stable, survey-unique question identifier. Referenced by logic jumpTo/conditions and used as the key in Response.data. Immutable once responses exist.

surveyStatus.$comment: MUST match models.md SurveyStatus. Public runtime serves only 'published'.

surveyLanguages.description: Declared languages. Exactly one MUST have default=true; its code is the i18n fallback and pairs with the 'default' i18nString key.

hiddenFields.description: Survey-level hidden fields (re-broadcast — parallel to the per-question `hidden` type, which remains for Formbricks-compat single-question prefills). Each entry declares a query-param key captured into the response at runtime: a URL like `?userId=123&plan=pro` populates the matching hidden field values into Response.data, where they become available to recall/piping (#recall:<key>/fallback:#) and to logic conditions. The `id` is the Response.data key + the recall lookup key; `name` is the human label shown in the builder. Ids must be unique across hidden fields AND must not collide with question ids (enforced in code, mirroring the unique-question-id check).

id.$comment: The query-param key AND the Response.data / recall lookup key. Reuses #/$defs/questionId so it shares the question-id charset and can be referenced by recall tokens the same way a question answer is.

name.description: Human-friendly label shown in the builder's Hidden fields section + recall insert list. Optional; defaults to the id.

variable.description: An author-defined survey variable (Formbricks parity). A named, typed mutable value seeded from `initialValue`; mutated by `calculate` logic actions as the respondent progresses; readable by recall tokens (#recall:<id>/...#) and logic conditions (leftQuestionId: <id>). `id` shares the question/ending/hidden-field id namespace (#/$defs/questionId charset) — it must be unique across that whole namespace (enforced in code, mirroring the unique-question-id check) so recall + condition refs resolve unambiguously.

id.$comment: The variable id AND its recall lookup key / condition leftQuestionId. Reuses #/$defs/questionId so it shares the id charset + namespace with questions/endings/hidden fields.

name.description: Human-friendly label shown in the builder's Variables panel + recall/calculate insert lists.

type.description: The variable's value type. number -> assign/add/subtract/multiply/divide; text -> assign/concat (#/$defs/action calculate.operation validity is enforced in-code).

initialValue.description: The variable's seed value (a number for type:number, a string for type:text — enforced by the type-conditional allOf below). Variable replay starts from this value each response.

quota.description: One response quota (survey `quotas[]`). Caps how many FINISHED responses matching `condition` are accepted; once `limit` matching finished responses exist, the next (Nth+1) matching respondent is marked over-quota at finalize and routed to `endingId` (or a built-in 'quota full' screen when absent). `condition` is a #/$defs/conditionGroup — the SAME boolean-tree shape logic rules + follow-up triggers use, evaluated by the SAME frozen evaluator against the final Response.data. Constraints jsonschema can't express (checked in-code by apps.surveys.quotas_validation.validate_quotas, mirroring follow-up cross-refs): unique quota ids; `endingId` resolves to a declared endings[].id; every condition `leftQuestionId` resolves to a real question/hidden-field id with a type-valid operator.

id.$comment: Stable, survey-unique quota id (reuses the question-id charset). Distinct namespace from questions/endings/hidden-fields/variables — a quota id is NOT a Response.data key or a recall/condition source, so it is NOT cross-checked against that id namespace; only uniqueness AMONG quotas is enforced.

name.description: Human label shown in the builder's Quotas section (internal only — no i18n). E.g. 'US respondents', 'Detractors'.

limit.description: Maximum number of FINISHED responses matching `condition` to accept. The (limit+1)th matching finished respondent is over-quota.

condition.description: The matching condition (a #/$defs/conditionGroup over the response answers + hidden fields, identical to logic conditions). A response counts toward this quota iff its final Response.data satisfies this condition (evaluated by the SAME Python/TS evaluator as logic, _eval_condition).

endingId.$comment: OPTIONAL: which ending screen to show an over-quota respondent. Must resolve to a declared endings[].id (enforced in-code: quota_unknown_ending). Absent -> the runtime shows a built-in 'quota full' screen (no survey ending needed).

calcValue.description: The right-hand operand of a `calculate` action: a typed LITERAL scalar, or a REF to a question answer / another variable / hidden field by id (all share the id namespace). The tagged shape removes the literal-vs-id ambiguity (is 'q1' the string "q1" or a reference to question q1?). The in-code validator + evaluator resolve a ref by id against the answers map enriched with the live variable values; an unresolved/empty/type-incompatible operand makes the calculate a deterministic no-op (the variable is left unchanged) — identical in TS and Python.

value.$comment: string for text ops; number for numeric ops (validity enforced in-code).

ref.$comment: An id in the shared namespace: a question id, another variable id, or a hidden-field id.

closeConditions.description: Auto-close rules. Either or both may be set. by_date closes after the timestamp; by_response_cap closes once finished responses reach the cap. null = no auto-close.

styling.description: Theming. All keys optional; runtime applies defaults. Colors are CSS color strings (#hex or rgb()).

followUp.description: One survey follow-up automation (the editor's 'Follow-ups' tab). On response finalize, if `trigger` fires (optionally gated by a `condition` over the answers), `action` runs — v1: send an email to a response-derived recipient. Re-broadcast structure: {id, name?, trigger, action}, mirroring #/$defs/ending's {id, type, ...} shape. `id` is stable + survey-unique (the FollowUpDelivery dedup key per response).

name.description: Human label shown in the builder list. Optional.

followUpTrigger.description: When a follow-up fires. v1 supports the 'responseFinished' event (fires on the finalize POST). An optional `condition` (a #/$defs/conditionGroup over the response answers + hidden fields, identical to logic conditions) gates the fire: absent/null condition = always fire on finish; present = fire only when it evaluates true against the final Response.data (evaluated by the SAME Python/TS evaluator as logic, _eval_condition).

condition.description: Optional gating condition. null/absent = unconditional (fire on every finish).

followUpAction.description: What a follow-up does. v1: type 'sendEmail' — render `subject` (i18nString + recall tokens) and `body` (HTML i18nString + recall tokens) against the response, resolve `recipient`, and enqueue the email via the existing email infra (apps.followups.tasks -> the shared send_mail_task / Postmark backend). Recall tokens (#recall:<id>/fallback:<text>#) in subject/body resolve against the final Response.data (answers + captured hidden fields) at send time.

subject.$comment: Email subject line; i18nString (default required). MAY embed recall tokens, resolved against Response.data at send time, then stripped of HTML (subjects are plain text).

body.$comment: Email body HTML; i18nString (default required). MAY embed recall tokens (resolved first) + a sanitized HTML subset (same allow-list as question descriptionHtml).

followUpRecipient.description:
Who receives a follow-up email. A DISCRIMINATED object (NOT a string overload — a fixed email like 'q1@x.com' must not collide with a question id 'q1'). Three forms:
- {type:'contact'} — the response's associated Contact's `email` attribute (server-derived from the SurveyLink, the only trusted contact source; rbac.md §11). No email on the contact -> no send (recorded skipped).
- {type:'fixedEmail', email} — a static address (e.g. an ops inbox).
- {type:'responseField', questionId} — the email the RESPONDENT typed: the answer at `questionId` (a contactInfo question's `email` sub-field, or an openText/contactInfo answer that is itself an email string). This is the 'respondent' recipient.

block.description: One question-grouping block (survey `blocks[]`). A block GROUPS a subset of the flat `questions[]` for display and OPTIONALLY randomizes the order in which its member questions are presented at runtime. It does NOT own the questions (they live in `questions[]`) and does NOT reorder the flat array — `questionIds` is a list of REFERENCES into `questions[]`. Constraints jsonschema can't express (checked in-code, mirroring follow-up cross-refs): each id in `questionIds` resolves to a real question; a question id appears in at most one block across the whole survey; block ids are unique.

id.$comment: Stable, survey-unique block id (reuses the question-id charset). Distinct namespace from questions/endings — a block id is NOT a Response.data key, so it is NOT cross-checked against the question/ending/hidden-field id namespace; only uniqueness AMONG blocks is enforced.

title.description: Human label shown on the block in the builder (e.g. 'Block 1', 'Demographics'). Optional; the builder defaults to 'Block N'.

questionIds.description: The member question ids, IN BUILDER DISPLAY ORDER (a presentation grouping, not the flow order — flow order is `questions[]`). Each entry MUST be a question id present in `questions[]`; a question id may appear in at most ONE block (enforced in-code). May be empty (an empty block is harmless — it groups nothing and randomizes nothing).

randomize.description: Within-block question-order randomization at runtime: 'none' (default — present member questions in `questions[]` flat order, byte-identical to no-block behavior), 'all' (shuffle all member questions), 'exceptLast' (shuffle all but the last member question, which stays pinned at the block's end). Seeded per-response (the response id) so the permutation is stable across back-navigation. Mirrors the per-question singleSelect/multiSelect `shuffle` enum.

questions.description: Ordered question array. Order defines linear flow; logic overrides via jumpTo. IDs must be unique (enforced in code: jsonschema cannot assert cross-item uniqueness of a nested key, so the Python/TS validators add a 'unique question ids' check — see REVIEW.md).

question.description: Discriminated union on 'type'. Common fields below; per-type config under oneOf.
question.$comment: INTENTIONAL: `additionalProperties` is deliberately omitted (i.e. left open) on the question object so new common question-level fields (e.g. future `recallInfo`, `imageUrl`) can be added without breaking older validators during the forward-compat window. Tightening is per-type instead: each `config` object under oneOf sets `additionalProperties: false`. Do not add `additionalProperties: false` here without a contract re-broadcast.

descriptionHtml.description: OPTIONAL rich-text question description (a SANITIZED HTML subset). RE-BROADCAST NOTE (backward-compatible additive field): when present + non-empty for the active language, the runtime renders this (sanitized) below the headline IN PLACE OF the plain `subheader`; absent it, behavior is unchanged (plain `subheader`). Allowed tags are b/strong/i/em/u/a[href]/br/p/ul/ol/li/span ONLY — every other tag, all event-handler attributes, and javascript:/data:/vbscript: hrefs are stripped at render time by the shared sanitizeHtml() helper (frontend/src/lib/sanitizeHtml.ts). Like other display strings it MAY embed recall tokens of the FROZEN form `#recall:<id>/fallback:<text>#`; tokens are resolved (resolveRecall) BEFORE sanitization so piped answer values cannot smuggle markup. Stored as an i18nStringOptional map (per-language descriptions).

logic.description: Ordered list of logic rules evaluated AFTER this question is answered. See #/$defs/logicRule and the evaluation-order note.

questionType.description: The 16 v1 question types + hidden fields. (Re-broadcast: added pictureChoice authoring + address + scheduleMeeting to reach Formbricks question-type parity.) FROZEN; adding a type is a contract re-broadcast.

isOther.description: If true, renders an 'Other' free-text input; answer captures the typed value.

config.$comment: NPS is always a fixed 0..10 scale (11 buttons). No range config. Analytics computes the NPS score from the 0..10 answer (detractors 0-6, passives 7-8, promoters 9-10).

q_cta.$comment: Statement / Call-to-Action. Displays content; optional external link. Not a data-collecting question unless 'required' (acts as an acknowledged gate). Answer is boolean (clicked/dismissed) or null.

label.$comment: The consent checkbox label, e.g. 'I agree to the terms'.

q_contactInfo.$comment: Contact-info composite. Each enabled sub-field collects a validated value; answer is an object keyed by sub-field. email/phone carry format validation.

q_address.$comment: Address composite (multi-subfield, mirrors contactInfo). Each enabled sub-field collects a plain-text value; answer is an object keyed by sub-field. Postal codes / regions are NOT format-validated (they vary by country) — values are plain text, like contactInfo's non-email fields.

addressSubField.$comment: An address sub-field (addressLine1/addressLine2/city/state/zip/country). Same shape as contactSubField.

q_scheduleMeeting.$comment: Schedule-a-meeting via a Cal.com inline embed. config.calLink is the cal.com path (username or username/event-type, e.g. 'jane' or 'jane/30min'). The runtime renders the inline embed; the answer records the booking ({booked:true, uid?}). Treated as object-shaped for logic (isSubmitted/isSkipped only).

calLink.description: cal.com path: 'username' or 'username/event-type'. Not a full URL — the embed prepends https://cal.com/.

q_hidden.$comment: Hidden field: not rendered. Value supplied via URL query param or single-use/per-contact link prefill. Stored in Response.data like any answer. Carries no UI; headline used only as an admin label.

fieldKey.description: Query-param / prefill key (e.g. 'utm_source'). Also the Response.data key if different from question id is desired; default key is the question id.

logicRule.description: A single logic rule attached to a question. If `condition` evaluates true against the response so far, `action` fires. Rules are evaluated top-to-bottom; see evaluation-order note in the action $comment.

conditionGroup.description: Boolean tree of conditions. Either a leaf (single condition) or a connector node with `connector` + `conditions`.

conditionLeaf.description: A single comparison against a question's answer. `operator` validity depends on the referenced question's type (see operator-validity table below). The evaluator (TS & Python) enforces operator/type validity; jsonschema only checks structure.

leftQuestionId.description: Question whose answer is the left operand. SHOULD reference a question at or before the rule's host question in linear order (forward refs are undefined at eval time and rejected by the validator).

value.description: Right operand. Type depends on operator/question: string|number|boolean for scalar comparisons; array for isOneOf/includesAll/includesAny; omitted for isSubmitted/isSkipped/isEmpty/isNotEmpty.

operator.description:
Comparison operators. OPERATOR-VALIDITY BY TYPE (enforced by evaluators + builder, per REVIEW.md):
- openText/contactInfo/address(text): equals, notEquals, contains, doesNotContain, startsWith, endsWith, isSubmitted, isSkipped, isEmpty, isNotEmpty
- singleSelect/pictureChoice(single): equals, notEquals, isOneOf, isSubmitted, isSkipped
- multiSelect/pictureChoice(multi): includesAll, includesAny, includesOnly, doesNotInclude, isSubmitted, isSkipped
- rating/nps/number: equals, notEquals, greaterThan, greaterThanOrEqual, lessThan, lessThanOrEqual, isOneOf, isSubmitted, isSkipped
- date: equals, notEquals, before, after, isSubmitted, isSkipped
- consent: isAccepted, isNotAccepted (boolean), isSubmitted, isSkipped
- cta: isClicked, isSkipped
- matrix/ranking/scheduleMeeting: isSubmitted, isSkipped (fine-grained operators deferred; scheduleMeeting's booking object is opaque)
operator.$comment: OPERAND TYPES for the equality-family operators (equals, notEquals, isOneOf): these operate on SCALARS (string/number/boolean) or ARRAYS OF SCALARS only — matching #/$defs/conditionLeaf 'value', which permits string|number|boolean|array|null but NOT object. An OBJECT-SHAPED answer (the answerShapes for contactInfo -> {firstName?,...}, address -> {addressLine1?,...}, matrix -> {rowId: columnId|[columnId]}, scheduleMeeting -> {booked,uid?}) is NOT a valid comparison target for these operators and deterministically DOES NOT MATCH: equals -> false, notEquals -> true (vacuously not-equal), isOneOf -> false. This holds IDENTICALLY in the TS and Python evaluators (no deep object comparison). This resolves the prior TS<->PY drift where Python deep-compared dicts while TS returned false (FU-1; pinned by the 'operators — equals/notEquals on a contactInfo (object-shaped) answer -> no-match (TS<->PY drift-guard)' fixture). Note: most equality-family-on-object-answer pairings are already rejected by validateSurvey's operator/type table (isOneOf is not a contactInfo/address operator; matrix/ranking/scheduleMeeting permit only isSubmitted/isSkipped), so the validator-reachable case is equals/notEquals on contactInfo/address (and hidden); the no-match rule above governs any object-shaped left operand should one reach the evaluator.

action.description:
What fires when a rule's condition is true. EVALUATION ORDER (frozen; implemented identically in TS runtime + Python):
1. The respondent answers question Q (or skips, if optional).
2. Q's `logic` rules are evaluated in array order against the full set of answers given so far (including Q's just-submitted answer).
3. The FIRST rule whose `condition` is true determines the navigation action (jumpTo / skip / endSurvey). 'require' actions are NOT navigation and are applied during answering (they make a target question required); all matching 'require' rules apply.
4. If no rule matches, advance to the next question in linear array order.
5. A jumpTo target must be a later question id or an ending id; backward jumps are rejected by the validator to guarantee termination.
6. 'skip' removes the named target question(s) from the path for THIS respondent; their Response.data keys are absent.
The shared fixture suite (REVIEW.md) encodes (survey_logic, answers) -> expected_next cases run in BOTH languages.

target.$comment: A later question id OR an ending id.

endingId.$comment: Optional: which ending screen to show. Defaults to the first ending.

target.$comment: Make this (later) question required for this respondent.

oneOf.$comment: calculate is a NON-NAVIGATION action (like require): it mutates a survey variable but does NOT decide the next step. During evaluation `firstMatchingNavAction` keeps scanning past it; all matching calculate rules on a host apply in array order (their mutations are visible to subsequent rules on the same host), and a matching navigation rule (jumpTo/skip/endSurvey) HALTS the scan (a calculate after a matched nav rule does not apply). `variableId` must resolve to a declared survey.variables[].id; `operation` must be valid for that variable's type (number -> assign/add/subtract/multiply/divide; text -> assign/concat — enforced in-code). `value` is a #/$defs/calcValue (literal scalar OR a ref by id). A divide-by-zero, a non-numeric numeric operand, or an unresolvable/empty/type-incompatible ref makes the calculate a deterministic NO-OP (variable unchanged) — identical in TS + Python.

operation.$comment: number variables: assign/add/subtract/multiply/divide. text variables: assign/concat. Operation/type validity is enforced in-code by validate_survey (the schema only checks the enum).

segmentFilter.description: Reusable contact filter stored on Segment.filter (models.md §2.13). Boolean tree of attribute conditions. Operators must be valid for the ContactAttributeKey.data_type (string|number|boolean|date) — same operator family as conditionLeaf, enforced in code.

answerShapes.$comment: NON-VALIDATING reference doc: the value stored in Response.data[questionId] per type. Used by analytics + the Python finalize validator (which checks answers against question type). openText/cta-> string|bool; singleSelect-> choiceId (or {choiceId, other} when isOther); multiSelect-> [choiceId]; pictureChoice-> choiceId (single) or [choiceId] (when allowMulti); rating-> integer 1..range; nps-> integer 0..10; consent-> boolean; date-> 'YYYY-MM-DD'; fileUpload-> [fileUrl]; number-> number; ranking-> [choiceId] ordered; matrix-> {rowId: columnId | [columnId]}; contactInfo-> {firstName?,lastName?,email?,phone?,company?}; address-> {addressLine1?,addressLine2?,city?,state?,zip?,country?}; scheduleMeeting-> {booked:true, uid?:string} once a meeting is booked; hidden-> string.

headline.default: Are you interested in a demo?

body.default: A respondent said they are interested. Reach out at #recall:email/fallback:(no email)#.
